name: Bhuvan Gupta
profile: Bhuvan Gupta is co-founder and CTO of OfBusiness, an Indian B2B platform that supplies raw materials and credit to small and medium businesses. He holds a B.E. from BITS Pilani and an MBA from FMS, University of Delhi, and worked at Snapdeal, Bharti SoftBank and Exponential before co-founding OfBusiness.
interesting_fact: Before OfBusiness he worked at three tech companies: Snapdeal, Bharti SoftBank (BSB) and Exponential, according to the company's own team page.
deep_cut_fact: He combines an engineering degree from BITS Pilani with an MBA from the Faculty of Management Studies (FMS), University of Delhi, and worked at Bharti SoftBank (BSB) before OfBusiness.
notes: The team page lists no press email (only getsupport@ofbusiness.in for customer support); its Press & Media section has a media kit. Aggregator sites call him ex-VP Engineering at Snapdeal, but that title is not on an official source.

name: Wen Bin (文宾)
profile: Wen Bin founded Wenheyou in Changsha. It began as a street fried-skewer stall in 2010 and grew into 'Super Wenheyou', large food-and-culture complexes that recreate 1980s city streets, with sites in Changsha, Guangzhou and Shenzhen. He has said he wants it to be 'the Disneyland of the restaurant industry'.
interesting_fact: In 2010, aged 22, Wen Bin quit a job paying 200,000 yuan a year to sell fried skewers from a street stall in Changsha. The name Wenheyou means 'Wen Bin and his friends'.
deep_cut_fact: From 2014 Wen Bin and Super Wenheyou GM Weng Donghua collected objects thrown away when old Changsha neighbourhoods were demolished, numbering and cataloguing them. Tens of thousands of these items now decorate Super Wenheyou, and the Changsha Haixin Plaza store won a Red Dot design award in 2019.
notes: No personal or press contacts found. Co-founder Yang Ganjun (杨干军) is the more public speaker. A 2025 trade report says Wenheyou pulled back from national expansion to focus regionally. No recent personal news on Wen Bin found, so alive is marked unknown (no reports of death).

name: Nick Grandy
current_role: Co-founder, Outschool (listed elsewhere as Head of Product; current title not confirmed)
profile: Nick Grandy co-founded Outschool, the San Francisco online marketplace for live small-group children's classes, in 2015 with Amir Nathoo and Mikhail Seregine. He came from Airbnb's engineering team. Outschool grew sharply during COVID and reached a $3B valuation in its October 2021 Series D. In February 2026 Nathoo stepped down as CEO and the COO and CTO took over as co-leaders.
interesting_fact: During COVID Outschool's business grew about 15x, and it went from 1,000 to 6,000 teachers in six months, Grandy said in a 2021 interview.
deep_cut_fact: Grandy was a high school teacher early in his career and then joined Airbnb's early team. He says Airbnb gave him his appreciation for peer-to-peer marketplaces, the model Outschool uses for education.
notes: Low public profile. Nathoo's February 2026 leadership-transition letter thanks Grandy as a co-founder but does not give his current role. Aggregator education details (Harvard/Oxford) were not verified and are left out.

name: Dain Sundstrom
current_role: Co-founder, IceGuard (stealth data-security startup); formerly co-founder and CTO of Starburst
profile: Dain Sundstrom is one of the four engineers who created the Presto distributed SQL engine at Facebook, starting in 2012. In 2018 they left and forked it as PrestoSQL, renamed Trino in 2020, and he co-founded Starburst, the commercial Trino company valued at $3B. In early 2025 he and David Phillips left Starburst to co-found IceGuard, a stealth data-security company.
interesting_fact: The four Presto creators left Facebook in 2018 after disagreements over Facebook's influence on Presto's governance, forked the code as PrestoSQL (now Trino), and reunited as Starburst's technical leadership.
deep_cut_fact: Before Presto he was in the Java open-source world: he is listed as an Apache committer in the Apache incubator proposal for OpenEJB, the EJB container used by the Apache Geronimo application server.
notes: Left Starburst in early 2025 (Blocks and Files, April 2025). IceGuard is in stealth, and no IceGuard website or contact was found. Active in the Trino open-source community, which is a possible route. Good fit for a data-infrastructure episode.

name: Chanakya Hridaya
current_role: Co-founder, Executive Director and COO, BlackBuck Limited (formerly Zinka Logistics Solutions), a listed company
profile: Chanakya Hridaya co-founded BlackBuck in Bengaluru in 2015 with Rajesh Yabaji and B. Ramasubramaniam. BlackBuck is a digital platform for India's truck operators, covering payments, telematics, freight marketplace and vehicle finance. It listed in India in 2024 and has since renamed itself from Zinka Logistics Solutions to BlackBuck Limited. Hridaya is an executive director and promoter.
interesting_fact: BlackBuck, which he co-founded, listed on Indian exchanges in 2024. Its investor-relations page publishes his employment agreement among the IPO material documents, and he is named as a promoter and executive director.
deep_cut_fact: Before BlackBuck he worked in ITC Limited's supply-chain division. He holds a B.Tech in mechanical engineering and a master's in manufacturing science and engineering from IIT Kharagpur (per his company bio as quoted).

public_contacts.value: cs@blackbuck.com (Company Secretary and Compliance Officer, shareholder queries)

notes: The deep-cut source is an aggregator that quotes his official bio. MarketScreener lists a different title (Chief Sales Officer), so check the role before outreach. Do not confuse him with a different Chanakya Hridaya linked to AlmaBetter. He appeared on The Desi VC podcast (episode 89, October 2022).

name: Shadiah Sigala
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Kinside (child-care benefits marketplace); co-founder, HoneyBook
profile: Shadiah Sigala moved from Mexico to southern California at age 7 and later studied at Pomona College and the Harvard Kennedy School. In 2013 she co-founded HoneyBook, the small-business client and finance management platform valued at more than $2B in 2021, with three Israeli entrepreneurs. In 2018 she co-founded Kinside, an employer child-care benefit marketplace, which acquired LegUp in 2022.
interesting_fact: She came to the US from Mexico at 7, the first in her family to go to college. She went from a $80K project-management job at Aetna to co-founding a $2B+ startup.
deep_cut_fact: Before tech, in 2010, she ran a personal-chef business, finding clients through her Pomona College alumni network. It supported her for about a year until she concluded 'My time doesn't scale.'
notes: Kinside's child-care focus also connects to her 2022 Kinside/LegUp press release (Business Wire). No current (2025-26) confirmation of her Kinside role was found. No published personal or press contacts were found; Kinside's website or PR is the likely route. She is open about her immigrant story and talks about it publicly (CNBC Make It, Pomona 'Sagecast').

name: Nate Baker
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Qualia (real-estate closing / title software)
profile: Nate Baker is co-founder and CEO of Qualia, a San Francisco software platform that title, escrow and real-estate companies use to run home closings (valued at about $2B per Hurun). He had started a small company in college and then worked at the venture fund 8VC before Qualia. Qualia has since grown past $100M ARR.
interesting_fact: Qualia was chosen by spreadsheet. Baker drew up 10 'selection heuristics' for an enduring B2B software market (platform not feature, network effects, multiple paths to revenue). The finalists were life-insurance broker software, P&C claims-adjusting software and title software.
deep_cut_fact: Qualia's first customer, Massachusetts state senator and real-estate lawyer Barry Feingold, was met at a conference thanks to a Stanford sweatshirt. Baker and Qualia's first 25 employees took turns living in Feingold's Andover basement to learn the title business, and new hires also tutored his kids in math.

public_contacts.value: Guest on The SaaS Podcast (SaaS Club) episode 467

notes: He speaks at industry events (ALTA) and on podcasts, so he is fairly accessible. No published press email was verified. Education (UPenn mechanical engineering) appears only on aggregator sites and is not verified here.

name: Jean-Gabriel Levon
current_role: Co-founder of Ÿnsect (insect protein; company in judicial liquidation since 1 Dec 2025). Previously listed as Chief Impact Officer and director. Current role unknown.
profile: Jean-Gabriel Levon (HEC Paris, École Polytechnique) co-founded Ÿnsect in Paris in 2011 with Antoine Hubert, Fabrice Berro and Alexis Angot. Ÿnsect farmed mealworms for animal-feed protein and fertilizer, raised about €600M and reached unicorn valuation. After safeguard and reorganisation proceedings, the Évry commercial court ordered its liquidation on 1 December 2025.
interesting_fact: In June 2020 Ÿnsect's insect-based fertilizer 'Ynfrass' received ANSES market approval, which Wikipedia describes as the first market approval in the world for a natural insect-based fertilizer.
deep_cut_fact: Ÿnsect was started in 2011 by four young scientists and environmental activists. Levon was the HEC/Polytechnique graduate among them, and an early 2013 Le Parisien headline described the startup as wanting to 'feed the planet with flies'.
notes: Sensitive: Ÿnsect was liquidated in December 2025 amid political criticism over about €148M of public funding, so avoid it as a hook. His current activity was not found (alive marked unknown, with no reports otherwise). Very low public profile; the 'Chief Impact Officer' title comes only from an aggregator.

name: Nicolas d'Audiffret
current_role: Co-founder, Ankorstore (co-led the company until 2025; Grégoire de Tilly named CEO in 2026)
profile: Nicolas d'Audiffret is a French serial marketplace founder. With Nicolas Cohen he co-founded ALittleMarket (2012), France's top handmade-goods marketplace, which Etsy bought in 2014. In 2019 he co-founded Ankorstore, a European B2B wholesale marketplace linking independent brands and shops, which raised over €365M and was valued at more than €1.7B in early 2022. He co-ran it until 2025.
interesting_fact: Ankorstore was born at Etsy. He and Nicolas Cohen worked there after the ALittleMarket sale, noticed Etsy sellers wanted to wholesale to shops, and after staying France-only with their first company, launched Ankorstore internationally from day one.
deep_cut_fact: Before becoming an entrepreneur he spent 2003-2011 as a consultant at Bain & Company in Paris and San Francisco. In 2026 Ankorstore's CEO role passed to another Bain alumnus, Grégoire de Tilly.

public_contacts.value: Guest episode: 'How To Build A $2 Billion Unicorn In Under 3 Years with Ankorstore's Nicolas d'Audiffret'

notes: No longer CEO. Consultor (2026) says he co-led Ankorstore until 2025, and his new activity was not found. Do not confuse him with co-founder Nicolas Cohen. He has done English-language podcasts and interviews. The podcast entry was taken from a search listing and was not opened.

name: Matthew McDonald
current_role: Co-founder and founding CTO, EquipmentShare (Nasdaq: EQPT). He stepped back from the CTO seat to an engineering role by 2019; current title not confirmed.
profile: Matthew McDonald is EquipmentShare's technology co-founder. At a Columbia, Missouri Startup Weekend he met the contractors behind the idea, built a prototype and booked a skid-loader rental the same weekend. The team went through Y Combinator, and EquipmentShare grew into a national construction-equipment rental and telematics company that IPO'd on Nasdaq in January 2026 at about a $6B valuation.
interesting_fact: Former co-worker Wade Foster, who went on to co-found Zapier, talked the team into applying to Y Combinator. McDonald admits he first dismissed YC as 'something for Silicon Valley people'.
deep_cut_fact: As founding CTO he grew the engineering team to 11, then with a mentor's help realised he did not enjoy the leadership seat and handed it over. His engineering team was remote from day one because his wife had just taken a job in Maine.
notes: The SEC filing names only the Schlacks brothers as co-founders, while Startland News lists McDonald among the co-founders (with Brad Siegler and Jeff Lowe). Low profile; his current role at EquipmentShare is unknown. IPO details (23 Jan 2026, $24.50/share, about $6B) come from search snippets of RER/IPOScoop.

name: Jonathan Winer
current_role: Co-founder and former co-CEO, Sidewalk Infrastructure Partners (no longer on SIP's team page, which lists Brian Barlow as Co-Founder and CEO). Current role unknown.
profile: Jonathan Winer is a former Alphabet/Sidewalk Labs executive who co-founded Sidewalk Infrastructure Partners (SIP) with Brian Barlow. SIP spun out of Alphabet in 2020 with a $400M Series A from Alphabet and Ontario Teachers'. It builds tech-enabled infrastructure platforms, and its current companies include Verrus (flexible, grid-friendly data centers) and Everyday Electric (residential virtual power plants).
interesting_fact: SIP's portfolio sits squarely in the energy and data-center space: Verrus builds next-generation data centers designed for flexibility, and Everyday Electric aggregates millions of households into virtual power plants.
deep_cut_fact: In SIP's first-ever interview (Fortune, May 2020) Winer pitched it as building 'unglamorous but sorely needed' infrastructure such as recycling sorting plants, consulting mayors rather than lobbying: 'We're not trying to sell our widgets.'

public_contacts.value: Guest on HASI 'Climate Positive' podcast E43 (March 2023)

notes: Highly relevant to energy and data-center themes (Verrus, VPPs). As of this check he is NOT listed on SIP's team page, so he has likely left SIP, and his new activity was not found; verify before outreach. Aggregators say he founded Nereus Capital, a private-equity firm, in 2010 (not verified here).

name: Hiroki Takeuchi
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, GoCardless, which now operates as 'GoCardless, a Mollie company' after Mollie completed its acquisition on 1 September 2026
profile: Hiroki Takeuchi co-founded London-based GoCardless, a bank-payments (direct debit / Pay by Bank) company, which went through Y Combinator and was valued at £1.55bn in 2022. GoCardless grew revenue 22% in FY25 and posted its first EBITDA-positive quarter. In September 2026 Dutch payments firm Mollie completed its acquisition of GoCardless, which keeps its brand under Takeuchi.
interesting_fact: After Mollie's acquisition, GoCardless keeps running as its own brand ('GoCardless, a Mollie company') under Takeuchi. The combined group serves 350,000+ businesses across 30+ markets, and GoCardless brings presence in the US, Canada, Australia and New Zealand.
deep_cut_fact: A line from Y Combinator stuck with him: Sam Altman described building a startup as 'riding a wave on a surfboard', where if you stay on the board you will eventually succeed and if you fall you can choose to get back on.
notes: GoCardless was acquired by Mollie (completed 1 Sep 2026), and Koen Köppen leads the group. Takeuchi is a regular speaker (London Tech Week, Paris Fintech Forum). Background details on aggregators (Oxford maths, McKinsey, co-founded 2011 with Tom Blomfield and Matt Robinson) were not verified on a primary source here.

name: Dan Littman
current_role: Helen L. and Martin S. Kimmel Professor of Molecular Immunology, NYU Grossman School of Medicine; HHMI Investigator; Pfizer board member; scientific co-founder of Immunai
profile: Dan R. Littman is a leading immunologist best known for cloning the CD4 and CD8 T-cell genes. He has been at NYU since 1995 and an HHMI investigator since 1987, and is a member of the National Academy of Sciences and National Academy of Medicine. He is a scientific co-founder and advisory board member of Immunai (AI and single-cell immune profiling) and Vedanta Biosciences, and sits on Pfizer's board.
interesting_fact: As a postdoc in Richard Axel's Columbia lab he cloned CD8 and, within months, CD4, the genes that define the two main types of T cells. CD4 later turned out to be HIV's receptor, and his lab's HIV work contributed to identifying CCR5 as a drug target, which Pfizer's maraviroc now blocks.
deep_cut_fact: He was born in Bucharest in 1952. His family waited years to emigrate, finally leaving Romania in 1962, and spent six months in Rome while his father passed the US medical licensing exam before they came to the US with help from HIAS.
notes: Primarily an academic scientist; Immunai is one of several company affiliations. The best route is his NYU lab. 'Pfizer's maraviroc' is my identification: the transcript says only 'Pfizer makes a drug' targeting CCR5.

name: Kevin Jones
current_role: Co-founder, Tarana Wireless (Milpitas, CA). MarketScreener lists him as VP Product Innovation 2009-2020; current role unknown.
profile: Kevin Jones is listed by financial-data aggregators as one of the 2009 founders of Tarana Wireless, a next-generation fixed-wireless broadband equipment maker, and as its VP of Product Innovation until 2020. Tarana's radios deliver high-speed non-line-of-sight broadband and cancel interference. The company has spent more than $400M in private R&D and is valued at about $1B+.
interesting_fact: Tarana's CEO told Congress in 2024 that the company was founded in 2009 by a wireless-industry veteran and three immigrant PhD students whose thesis was about bringing internet access to villagers in Ghana. Its radios adapt to channel conditions 5,000 times a second.
notes: Very little public information. His founder status comes only from aggregators (MarketScreener: founder and VP Product Innovation 2009-2020), and no official Tarana page naming him could be loaded (site returns 403). Common name, so take care not to confuse him with other Kevin Joneses (e.g. KORE Wireless). Low priority.
